# Volume 2 — XV The Beginning of Vacation

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The evening was calm and yellow, with winds murmuring in the spruces encircling the playground and long, idle shadows stretching near the forest’s border, as Nell locked the door of the schoolhouse. Contentment marked her sigh when she slipped the key into her pocket. Her teaching year had come to a close, and she had been rehired for the upcoming one amidst numerous compliments. . . . merely Mr. Gorham Pullen advised that she should apply the strap more frequently . . . while two charming months of earned time off called out to her enticingly. Carrying her flower basket down the hill, Nell experienced harmony with both her surroundings and herself. Ever since the first mayflowers bloomed, Nell had faithfully undertaken her weekly trip to the burial place of Obed. Quiet, reserved, insignificant Obed Abernethy had been erased from the minds of all other Brierley residents, Thirza excluded; yet Nell held his memory fresh within her heart, where it would remain forever. She was incapable of forgetting the gentle elder who was the initial person to offer the affection and understanding her deprived youth had yearned for.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0000 }

Where the hill ended, a boy sat upon the fence within the spruces’ shade . . . a boy possessing large, dreamy eyes alongside a lovely, sensitive countenance. Swinging himself down, he approached Nell with a smile; yet his cheeks bore the marks of tears.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0001 }

“Since I knew you were headed to the cemetery, teacher, I decided to wait for you,” he said, sliding his hand inside hers. “I’m heading there as well . . . This bouquet of geraniums is being brought by me to place on Grandpa Stanhope’s grave on behalf of grandma. And see, teacher, beside Grandpa’s grave I intend to place this bunch of white roses in memory of my little mother. . . since travelling to her grave to place it there is impossible for me. But don’t you believe she’ll be aware of it all, anyway?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0002 }

“Yes, I am sure she will, Cedric.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0003 }

“You understand, teacher, it is exactly three years to this day from when my little mother passed away. It is a very, very lengthy duration yet the pain is every bit as strong as always . . . and my longing for her is just as great as ever. At times I feel as though I am simply unable to endure it, the ache is so deep.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0004 }

Cedric spoke with a shaking voice, his lip quivering. Hoping his eyes' tears would go unseen by his teacher, he directed his gaze downward toward his roses.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0005 }

“And even so,” Nell murmured in a very quiet voice, “you would not desire the pain to cease . . . you would not choose to lose the memory of your little mother even were it possible.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0006 }

“No, truly, I would not . . . I perceive it in precisely that manner. You possess such a talent for comprehension, teacher. No one else comprehends as effectively . . . not even grandma, even though she treats me with such kindness. Father comprehended fairly well, yet I remained unable to converse with him extensively concerning mother, since it caused him such deep distress. Whenever he placed his hand across his countenance, I was invariably aware that I ought to cease speaking. Poor father, he undoubtedly feels terribly lonely lacking my company; however you see he possesses only a housekeeper at present and he believes housekeepers are unsuitable for raising small boys, particularly when his business requires him to remain away from home so frequently. Grandmothers excel further, second only to mothers. One day, once I am raised, I shall return to father and we shall never suffer separation again.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0007 }

Cedric had spoken to Nell regarding his mother and father to such an extent that she felt as though they were already familiar to her. In terms of temperament and disposition, she believed that his mother had likely closely resembled what he was himself; furthermore, it was her impression that Stephen Stanhope was a somewhat reserved individual possessing a deep and tender nature that he meticulously concealed from the public.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0008 }

“It isn’t very easy to get acquainted with Father,” Cedric had remarked on one occasion. “I didn’t become really acquainted with him until my little mother had died. However, once you do come to know him, he is splendid. I love him most of all in the world, and then Grandma Stanhope, and after that, you, teacher. Were it not my obligation to love Grandma Stanhope next to father on account of everything she is doing for me, I would love you second to him. You understand, teacher. Still, I wish that she would keep the lamp inside my room until I fall asleep. The moment she tucks me in, she takes it straight away, stating that I must not be a coward. Although I am not frightened, I would prefer to have the light. My little mother always used to sit next to me while holding my hand until I fell asleep. I suppose that she spoiled me. You know how mothers do at times.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0009 }

No, this was not known to Nell, even if it could be imagined by her. Sooly, she gave thought to her “little mother,” that same mother who had considered her to be so “perfectly beautiful” and who, having passed away so long ago, lay buried next to her boyish husband in a distant, unvisited grave. Because Nell had no memory of her mother, she came close to envying Cedric.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0010 }

“The coming week brings my birthday,” Cedric mentioned while the pair strolled up the lengthy red hill, enjoying the sunshine of June, “and a letter from father told me he is shipping a present he believes I will prefer above all other possible gifts. My opinion is that it arrived already, because Grandma keeps the drawer of the bookcase locked, which is a novel habit. Also, upon my asking her the reason, she merely appeared enigmatic and remarked that young boys should not possess excessive curiosity. Having a birthday causes great excitement, doesn’t it? Eleven will be my age. Looking at me, you would not suspect it, would you? According to Grandma I am quite tiny for my years, and she blames my insufficient consumption of porridge. Although I try as hard as I can, Grandma serves such large portions . . . Grandma is certainly not stingy, I assure you. From the time you and I discussed prayer on our way back from Sunday School that afternoon, teacher . . . when you advised that we should pray regarding every one of our troubles . . . my nightly prayer has been for God to grant me sufficient grace so I can consume every single scrap of my morning porridge. However, I have not managed it so far, and I truly am unable to determine if the cause is an insufficiency of grace or a surplus of porridge. Grandma states that father was raised on porridge, and the results were certainly excellent for him, since you should observe his broad shoulders. Even so,” Cedric finished, sighing with a thoughtful expression, “I genuinely believe porridge will prove to be my demise.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0011 }

Because Cedric’s eyes were turned away, Nell allowed a smile to touch her face. Throughout Brierley, it was common knowledge that ancient Mrs. Stanhope was raising her grandson by adhering to traditional, time-tested principles regarding moral conduct and eating habits.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0012 }

“Dear, we should wish that won't happen,” she remarked in a bright tone. “What progress are you making with your rock people? Is the senior Twin maintaining his good behavior?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0013 }

“It is necessary for him to do so,” Cedric declared with force. “He understands that I will refuse to be seen with him unless he complies. I believe he is truly steeped in evil.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0014 }

“And is Nora aware of the Golden Lady by now?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0015 }

“No; yet I believe she has an inkling. It is my near certainty that she observed me when I previously visited the cave. Her discovery of it would not bother me . . . my desire for her not to know exists solely on her account . . . to prevent her emotions from being wounded. However, should she be intent on suffering hurt feelings, it is unavoidable.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0016 }

“Do you believe that I might also behold your rock people if I went down to the beach with you one evening?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0017 }

Cedric solemnly moved his head from side to side.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0018 }

“No, it doesn't seem to me that my rock people would be visible to you. Only I am able to see them. However, it would be possible for you to view your own rock people. You belong to the type of person who is capable of it. The two of us are both that type. You know, teacher,” he continued, pressing her hand in a friendly way. “Is it not wonderful that we are that type, teacher?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0019 }

“Splendid,” agreed Nell, whose shining gray eyes peered down into the shining blue ones. It was known to both Nell and Cedric
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0020 }

“What a beautiful world Imagination reveals to our sight,”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0021 }

and each was aware of the path leading to that blissful realm. In that place, by valley and brook, the rose of happiness flowered eternally; the bright sky was never shadowed by clouds; melodious bells were never dissonantly out of harmony; and like-minded souls were plentiful. Understanding the location of that country . . . “east o’ the sun, west o’ the moon” . . . constitutes invaluable wisdom, impossible to purchase in any bazaar. The benevolent fairies must bestow it when one is born, and time is unable to spoil or deprive one of it. Possessing it while residing in an attic surpasses being a dweller of mansions lacking it.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0022 }

The Brierley cemetery remained the overgrown, deserted spot it had ever been. Naturally, the Improvers were paying attention to it, and Honora Hollis had given a presentation regarding graveyards at the previous gathering of the Society. Eventually, the Improvers intended for a tidy wire fence to take the place of the old, crooked board enclosure covered in lichen, as well as for the lawn to be trimmed and the tilting tombstones set upright.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0023 }

Nell placed the blossoms she had carried for Obed’s grave upon it, and subsequently crossed to the small, poplar-canopied spot where Dinah Wren reposed. Continuously from the date of the spring picnic, Nell had set blossoms upon Dinah’s grave whenever she paid a visit to Obed’s. During the previous evening, she had undertaken a journey back to the small, abandoned forest garden and retrieved a few of Dinah’s personal white roses from that location.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0024 }

“I believed you would prefer them over all the rest, my love,” she murmured gently.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0025 }

A shadow covered the grass while Nell remained seated there, and raising her eyes, she saw Mrs. Wace. Side by side, they made their way back home.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0026 }

The face belonging to Mrs. Wace no longer resembled that of the young bride whom Brierley had seen the minister bring five years earlier. A portion of its youthful roundness and bloom was gone, with delicate, enduring lines appearing around her mouth and eyes. A small grave located in the selfsame cemetery explained a few of those marks; others had newly formed while her young son was lately sick, a trial that had now fortunately passed. Even so, the dimples Mrs. Wace possessed remained just as charming and quick to appear as before, while her eyes stayed every bit as bright, clear, and honest; moreover, any lost maidenly attractiveness was presently far surpassed by an increase in strength and gentleness.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0027 }

“I assume you are anticipating your break, Nell?” she remarked, while they departed from the cemetery.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0028 }

Nell gave a nod.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0029 }

“Yes. . . . I could savor the word like a delicious delicacy beneath my tongue. I believe the summer will be wonderful. To begin with, Mrs. Varley is visiting the Island in July, and Honora will be bringing her here. Just thinking about it gives me one of my familiar ‘thrills.’”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0030 }

“I wish that you enjoy yourself, Nell. You have labored extremely hard over this previous year and you have achieved success.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0031 }

“Oh, I am not sure. In numerous ways, I have fallen very far short. My intentions when I started teaching this past autumn remain unaccomplished. My ideals have not been met by my actions.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0032 }

“None of us ever do,” Mrs. Wace said, sighing. “However, Nell, you are aware of Lowell’s words, ‘Not failure but low aim is crime.’ Ideals are necessary, and we must strive to fulfill them, even though complete success eludes us. Without them, life would prove to be a dismal affair. With them, it becomes magnificent and splendid. Keep a firm grip on your ideals, Nell.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0033 }

“I will attempt it. However, I must abandon the majority of my ideas,” stated Nell, with a faint laugh. “When I first began working as a teacher, I possessed the finest collection of ideas you could imagine, yet each single one has proved useless to me during various difficult moments.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0034 }

“Likewise the doctrine regarding physical discipline,” Mrs. Wace unitized playfully.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0035 }

However, Nell turned red.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0036 }

“For giving Anthony a whipping, I will never pardon myself.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0037 }

“Foolishness, my love, the punishment was well-merited by him. Furthermore, it did him good. Ever since, he has given you no grief, and he has been persuaded that you are second to none. His affection was earned by your gentleness once the notion that a ‘girl was useless’ had been eradicated from his obstinate brain.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0038 }

“Although he might have been deserving of it, that misses the main issue. Had my choice to lash him been made in a calm and considered manner out of a belief that he merited such chastisement, my feelings about the matter would be different. However, the reality, Mrs. Wace, remains that I simply lost my composure and struck him as a result. Considerations of justice or injustice never crossed my mind . . . I would have carried it out regardless of his innocence. My humiliation stems from that fact.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0039 }

“Well, we all commit errors, dear, so simply leave it in the past. We ought to feel remorse for our errors and draw lessons from them, yet not bear them ahead into the coming days with us. Yonder travels Hugh Carrow upon his bicycle . . . returning to his house for his holiday as well, I assume. In what manner are you and he progressing in your schoolwork?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0040 }

“Fairly well. Our intention is to complete the Virgil this evening . . . merely twenty lines remain. After that, our studies will pause until September.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0041 }

“Is it your belief that you will one day attend college?”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0042 }

“Oh, I don’t know.” Gazing dreamily off toward the horizon colored like an opal, Nell remarked. “Although we feel such gratitude in believing that Thirza’s eyes will fail no further, they are unlikely to ever improve significantly from their current state. Furthermore, regarding the twins . . . I have a feeling their uncle will not actually summon them at any point. College might lie past the turn in the path, yet having not reached that turn myself, I refrain from dwelling on it to avoid becoming dissatisfied.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0043 }

“Well, I would be pleased to see you attend college, Nell; however, if you fail to go, do not feel dissatisfied regarding it. In the end, we fashion our own existence no matter where we find ourselves . . . college merely assists us in accomplishing this with greater ease. Our lives become wide or restricted based upon what we invest in them, rather than what we extract. Existing is abundant and complete in this place . . . in all places . . . provided we are able to discover the way to unlock our entire hearts to its abundance and completeness.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0044 }

“I believe I grasp your meaning,” Nell remarked contemplatively, “and I am aware that I have a great deal to be grateful for . . . oh, a great deal . . . my employment, alongside Cedric Stanhope, as well as the beloved twins, plus every one of my friends. Are you aware, Mrs. Wace, that I am extremely grateful for friendship? It enhances life to such a degree.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0045 }

“A genuinely supportive element is found in authentic friendship,” remarked Mrs. Wace, “and our standards for it ought to be extremely elevated, avoiding any tarnishing caused by a lack of truthfulness and sincerity. It concerns me that the term friendship is frequently lowered to describe a form of closeness that contains no genuine friendship whatsoever.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0046 }

“Yes . . . similar to Tibby Tulk’s and Julia Bell’s. They share a close bond and accompany each other everywhere; yet Tibby continually utters unkind remarks about Julia when she is absent, and everyone believes she harbors jealousy toward her since she displays such delight whenever anyone finds fault with Julia. It seems to me a desecration to bestow the name of friendship on such a connection. Should we possess friends, our duty is to search solely for their finest qualities and offer them the finest qualities within ourselves, do you not agree? Were that so, friendship would become the loveliest reality on earth.”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0047 }

“Amity is truly lovely,” Mrs. Wace grinned, “yet eventually . . .”
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0048 }

Afterward, she stopped suddenly. Beside her, the refined, fair-browed face, possessing frank eyes and expressive features, remained much more that of a child than a woman. Only visions of companionship and aspiration were contained within Nell’s heart at this point, and Mrs. Wace had no desire to spoil the freshness of her gentle innocence. Consequently, she permitted the coming years to complete her thought.
{: #nw-v02-c15-p0049 }
